_comment: Register field positions measured on physical silicon where the device header and the reference manual disagree. pipeline/extract/rm/extract_registers.py appends the measurement to the evidence row's basis as `<method>:<probe>(=<bits>)`; the row stays `conflict` because the documents still disagree. pipeline/build/build_index.py adopts the measured bits in index/registers.csv (the same rule as F-41, where the index takes the RM grid's value). This file never creates a field; it only settles a position a document already states. An entry with "writable": false (and no bits) records that a field both documents define could not be written on silicon: the evidence row gets `!<method>:<probe>(writable=0)` and becomes `conflict`, and the index keeps the documented bits.

measured.how: ch32rv wrote option bytes data0=0x5a, data1=0xc3 on a CH32L103C8T6, then FLASH_OBR (0x4002201C) read 0x0c35acfc: [19:12]=0x5a, [27:20]=0xc3; the header's [17:10]/[25:18] would give 0x6b/0x0d. The same procedure on V203 (0x030d68fc) and V003 (0x030d6bdc) gives 0x5a/0xc3 at [17:10]/[25:18].

ch32rv core unlocked CMP_CTLR with CMP_KEY on a CH32V205RCT6, wrote 1 to bits 19, 29 and 30 and read back: bits 19 and 29 kept the value, bit 30 stayed 0. RM 23.3.4 (the CMP_CTLR figure) places HYS1_H at 19 and HYS2_H at 29 with 30 reserved; the EVT header ch32v205.h defines HYS1_H=0x20000000 (29) and HYS2_H=0x40000000 (30).
